findings.title: Shard-split queries are interpolated twice, once per shard group
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() now interpolates every target with datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters), and splitQueriesByStreamShard() then passes each shard sub-request to runSplitQuery(), which interpolates the same targets again with the same scopedVars and filters. The updated shard test confirms this: one original query now causes applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times. applyTemplateVariables is not just placeholder substitution for dashboard variables; it also applies request.filters/ad-hoc filters and variable formatting/escaping. Re-applying it can duplicate ad-hoc filters in the LogQL expression and can re-expand $-sequences introduced by the first replacement, corrupting the query or changing the stream selector, in addition to repeating the work for every shard group. Interpolation should happen once, e.g. runSplitQuery needs a way for the shard path to indicate targets are already interpolated.

findings.title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting() can defeat the $__range split guard
findings.body: Queries are now interpolated on line 299 before partition() calls querySupportsSplitting() on line 300. querySupportsSplitting() deliberately refuses to split queries containing $__range, $__range_s, or $__range_ms because those macros must be evaluated against the final request range (see the comment at lines 285-287). If applyTemplateVariables resolves those range macros from the request scoped vars, the token is gone by the time the guard runs, so a query that must not be split is split into daily chunks while keeping the full-range macro value baked into each chunk. That changes rate/count_over_time semantics at chunk boundaries and can return incorrect data. The range-variable check needs to run on the pre-interpolation expression, or range macros must be excluded from this early interpolation.

findings.title: Queries that interpolate to an empty expression are no longer filtered out
findings.body: The empty-expression filter runs before interpolation (lines 296-299), so a target whose whole expression is a variable, e.g. expr='$var', passes the filter and only becomes '' after applyTemplateVariables. Such a target is then classified and grouped as a normal (metric) query and sent downstream with an empty expression. If all targets interpolate to empty, runSplitQuery builds zero grouped requests and runSplitGroupedQueries() dereferences requests.filter(...)[0].partition after Math.max(...[]) , throwing a TypeError instead of completing with no data. The same regression is introduced in runShardSplitQuery(), which changed from interpolate-then-filter to filter-then-interpolate. Targets need to be filtered again after interpolation.
